text:
Erik Haula faces Nashville tonight for the first time since leaving after 132 games in two stints with the Predators. He's 35, on his eighth NHL team, and in Los Angeles the role is clear: a depth center at 15 minutes a night.

He has seven points in 15 games, including a goal and an assist in the 7-2 win over San Jose, and his finishing is right on his chances (three goals on 2.8 expected). The problem is the chance share. The Kings have only 35% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 19 points worse than without him, the worst relative mark on the team.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with penalties costing him and opponents creating more with him on the ice. He was a seventh-round pick in 2009 who has lasted past 850 games, which says something about how coaches see him. Our projection sees about 16 goals, but his line is the one the Kings most need to fix.
